data.name: Darshana
data.gender_notes: Darshana is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who gives a divine view or vision. A seer, a beholder, a witness. Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘drsh’, meaning to see. In Hindu mythology, Darshana refers to the divine vision granted to the devotees upon attaining spiritual enlightenment. The name Darshana carries the meaning “View, Sight, Vision” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Darshana usually hope their child will grow to embody view, sight, vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner wisdom and insight.
data.etymology: Darshana belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “View, Sight, Vision.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darshana total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Darshana" carries a profound cultural significance in Hinduism, symbolizing the power of divine vision and the importance of spiritual enlightenment. In various Hindu practices, seeking darshan or a divine vision of a god or goddess is considered an essential component of devotion. Seventeen sacred places, known as shrines, are considered highly auspicious for this purpose, with Tirumala Tirupati Balaji Temple in Andhra Pradesh, India, being the most renowned one. The ritual of darshan involves seeking the blessings of the deity, receiving their divine gaze and absorbing their transcendental energy. The custom of offering food and other offerings is a significant aspect of the darshan process.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Darshana" holds great spiritual significance, as it conveys the essence of the journey towards self-realization and self-awareness, which is the ultimate goal within Hindu spirituality. Achieving spiritual enlightenment through dedicated practice and wisdom is believed to grant one the ability to see beyond the material world, attain inner peace and attain Moksha or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Darshana, the divine vision, is the light that illuminates the path towards self-realization and provides the true meaning of life. Thus, the name is not just a moniker, but a manifestation of the deepest longing and aspiration for the self-realization and peace that comes with a true understanding of the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Darshana symbolizes the divine vision of perceiving the inner truth and beauty of the self and the universe. It is the act of seeing beyond the physical form and recognizing the divine essence within.

vedic_reference.note: Darshana is a Sanskrit name derived from the root word 'darshana' which means 'to see' or 'vision'. In Hindu mythology, Darshana is also associated with the various forms of God, including Durga and Shiva. It is also a name for the goddess of sight and vision.

historical_references.reference: Darshana was a famous Indian philosopher and scholar of the Nyaya and Vaisheshika schools of Hindu philosophy in the 2nd century BCE.

trends: used as a given name for girls
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Darshana remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Devi Darshana, a teacher in Delhi, India, shares that their name Darshana meaning "View, Sight, Vision" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
